input.summary:
Bedroom 2 is NOT lit. Its interior air is owned by the shell (shell.mjs fills the box with air), so runParts refuses every lantern written into it (probe: both spots refused, parts-report refusedAt shows "lantern -> air"). room-16.mjs is unchanged (empty stub, byte-identical to the original).
Measured alternative: standing lanterns at (31,11,40) and (33,11,40) on the upper porch deck clear every dark cell (min 2, mean 6.3, 0 dark, 39 dim) but do not reach 8+. Not written: the porch is room-28's cells, and touching it was out of scope.
Current build.nbt (rebuilt clean, make.sh OK): bedroom 2 has 10 dark cells (mob spawn) and 48 dim.
left: Bedroom 2 still has 10 dark cells (light 0) and 48 dim cells. Lanterns inside the room are refused by the lock, so 8+ cannot be reached from inside. Decision needed: (a) the shell stops filling room interiors with air, so room parts can own their lamps and furniture (shell.mjs line 27 `fill(..., "air")`), or (b) accept the two porch lanterns at (31,11,40) and (33,11,40) as a partial fix. Option (b) belongs to the upper porch part (room-28), so I did not write it.
room-16.mjs says its layout is kept in room-16.removed-writes.txt; that file does not exist. The bed, chests, desk, rug and lamps the designer asked for are gone, so there is nothing to light yet.
27 of 37 room parts placed 0 blocks with no refusals (empty stubs such as bedroom 5 and the upper hall). I did not investigate them; they may have the same problem.
Scratch probes were written under /tmp/lamp-scratch only. No project file other than build.nbt (rebuilt clean) was changed.

waste.what: Found the lock by writing two probe lanterns into room-16.mjs, rebuilding, and reading parts-report.json refusedAt, then restoring the file.
waste.cost: One full make.sh run plus a restore and a second clean make.sh.
waste.tool: `mcd room` (or `mcd check`) should name cells owned by an earlier part, e.g. "owned by mansion shell (air)", and a `--try x,y,z:block` overlay should test a block without editing the part.

waste.what: Tested porch lantern spots by hand: a scratch loader script, copies of build.nbt, and several variants; two runs failed on bad argument parsing.
waste.cost: About six scratch builds and light measurements, with 3 failed runs.
waste.tool: `mcd light build.nbt --add 31,11,40:lantern --add 33,11,40:lantern --rooms rooms.json --only "bedroom 2"` as an overlay that measures the light without writing a file.

waste.what: Worked out which cells the shell owns (the whole room box is one fill of air), by reading shell.mjs.
waste.cost: One file read plus the lock code in build.mjs.
waste.tool: `parts-report.json` should list owned cell counts per room box, so a designer can see that the room is locked before writing code.

companions.task: Build the bedroom's bed, dresser, desk and chair from room-16's layout once the shell releases the room's air. The removed writes are missing, so the layout must be rewritten.
Hang or stand the porch lanterns at (31,11,40) and (33,11,40), in the upper porch part's own code, and then add the interior lamps once the room is open.
